subject: Creativity
title: Inclusive Design: Building for Everyone by Designing for the Edges
description: A short lesson to help you apply Inclusive Design: Building for Everyone by Designing for the Edges.

hook.text: Closed captions were designed for deaf users. Now they're used by millions in noisy gyms, quiet offices, and bedrooms.

buildup.text: Inclusive design creates solutions for people with the most extreme constraints — then discovers those solutions help.

discovery.text: Microsoft's inclusive design toolkit identifies three types of exclusion: permanent (one arm), temporary (broken arm).

twist.text: Designing for one-armed use helps amputees, people with injuries, and anyone carrying a baby or groceries.

climax.text: Voice interfaces, dark mode, autocomplete, and touch screens all originated from accessibility needs.

punchline.text: Design for exclusion. Innovation for everyone follows.

quiz.question: What are Microsoft's three types of exclusion in inclusive design?
